title: Evaluate style-testing efficacy with a fixture-based blind A/B harness
description:
## Why (Computational)

Part 1 (tadw-wdk) can prove style-testing is correct-by-construction, wired, and reachable. It
cannot prove it is useful. The central risk Part 1 names is that the core "reduces to platitudes
once the framework nouns are removed", and Part 1 ships no detector for that: its gates check
token hygiene and invocation, not whether the skill changes the tests a model actually writes.

A prompt document with no behavioral evaluation is an unverified claim. The stakeholder is the
owner, who will otherwise adopt this skill across every language they work in on the strength of
its prose alone, and any future editor, who needs a regression signal before changing its wording.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing-part-2.md (M5b)

## Estimated size
9 files (4 fixture sources, 4 rubrics, 1 protocol), about 340 LOC, plus 36 model runs for tier 2
and 4 probes for tier 3. Band: Target.
design:
Four fixtures, one per framework the appendix covers: pytest, Vitest, XCTest, Minitest. Each
source file is 40 to 80 lines containing a happy path, an error path, a boundary condition, and at
least two nondeterminism traps (an injectable clock, an unordered collection, a record best
located by unique key). Each rubric.md holds 10 binary criteria derived from the 14 principles.

D8, trap subset. Three of the 10 criteria are pre-registered, before any run, as the ones an
unguided model reliably fails. They carry the discriminating weight. This exists because current
models write decent tests unprompted: if baseline already scores 8 or 9 of 10, a "strictly greater
in aggregate" bar is unachievable through no fault of the skill, and invites exactly the
bar-lowering the plan warns against.

D9, blind per-criterion judging. A third subagent sees both suites labeled A and B in randomized
order and scores each criterion independently with cited evidence. The treatment suite is often
self-identifying through its scenario naming and hoisted setup, so the blinding limitation is
stated in eval-protocol.md rather than claimed away. Per-criterion scoring with evidence is robust
to a judge who guesses the arm; a holistic preference score is not.

D10, smoke check first. One arm-pair per fixture (12 runs) gates the full 36-run matrix. A fixture
whose baseline passes all three traps is a broken fixture, not a null result, and is redesigned
before the full matrix runs.

Pass bar, all four must hold: treatment median at least 8 of 10 on every fixture; treatment at
least equal to baseline on every fixture; treatment strictly greater than baseline on the trap
subset on every fixture; zero framework-inappropriate advice.

Tier 3 after tier 2 clears: unseen-framework probe (Go testing, deliberately absent from the
appendix), RSpec non-regression diffed against the pre-rewrite SHA captured in Part 1's M2,
escape-hatch probe, and live dogfood writing real tests in a real project and running them.

A failing fixture produces a finding and a follow-up bead against the skill's wording. The bar is
never adjusted to fit the result.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the four fixtures each carry a rubric.md with 10 binary criteria, when inspected before any eval run, then exactly 3 criteria per fixture are marked as the pre-registered trap subset.
2. Given the smoke check (one arm-pair per fixture, 12 runs), when run, then no fixture's baseline passes all 3 trap criteria; any fixture that does is redesigned before the full matrix.
3. Given the full tier-2 matrix, when scored, then treatment median is at least 8 of 10 on every fixture, at least equal to baseline on every fixture, and strictly greater than baseline on the trap subset on every fixture.
4. Given the tier-2 results, when reviewed, then zero treatment outputs contain advice inappropriate to that fixture's framework.
5. Given the tier-3 unseen-framework probe against Go's testing package, when a model applies style-testing, then the output applies the core principles and invents no idiom from a different language.
6. Given the tier-3 RSpec non-regression probe diffed against the pre-rewrite SHA from Part 1's M2, when compared, then the post-rewrite output is at least as good as the pre-rewrite output.
7. Given the tier-3 dogfood, when the generated tests are run in a real project, then they pass.
8. Given eval-protocol.md, when read, then it states the blinding limitation explicitly rather than claiming the judge cannot infer the arm.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- skills/style-testing/references/fixtures/ holds 4 fixture directories, each with a source file and a 10-criterion rubric marking 3 traps.
- skills/style-testing/references/eval-protocol.md documents the arms, the blind judging procedure, the stated blinding limitation, and the pass bar.
- The 12-run smoke check passes and confirms every fixture's traps discriminate.
- The full tier-2 matrix clears all four pass-bar conditions.
- All four tier-3 probes pass, including live dogfood tests that actually run green.

## Scope boundary
Changing the skill's content in response to eval results is OUT of scope. A failing fixture
produces a finding and a follow-up bead, so the eval stays an honest measurement rather than
something the skill is tuned against.

title: Fix false plugin.json component-registration claims in AGENTS.md
description:
## Why (Computational)

AGENTS.md makes three false claims about .claude-plugin/plugin.json:

- Line 355: plugin.json "defines plugin metadata, component registration, and the hooks field"
- Line 529 (Adding a New Skill): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"
- Line 537 (Adding a New Agent): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"

plugin.json is 511 bytes containing name, version, description, author, license, and hooks. It
registers zero components. `grep -c "style-python\|style-frontend\|review-python"
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` returns 0. Skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their
directories; the real registration surfaces are the AGENTS.md component lists and the README table.

This is not cosmetic. The defect already produced an unsatisfiable acceptance criterion in this
tracker: bead tadw-wdk's original AC #3 required `grep -rw style-testing
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to match, which can never pass. Every agent or human who follows
AGENTS.md to add a component will keep generating the same bad work item until the instruction is
corrected. The stakeholder is anyone extending this plugin, including future agent sessions.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing-part-2.md (M4)

## Estimated size
1 file, about 6 lines changed. Band: below Target. Justified as a standalone bead because it is
independent of all style-testing work and blocks nothing.
design:
Fix the instruction, not just the description (D11). Correcting line 355 alone would leave 529 and
537 still telling readers to edit plugin.json, and those two lines are what actually caused the
defect.

- Line 355: state that skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their directories,
  and that plugin.json carries metadata plus the hooks field only.
- Lines 529 and 537: replace "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed" with the true
  surfaces, namely the AGENTS.md component lists and the README.md table.

Sequence after Part 1 (tadw-wdk). Part 1's M3 also edits AGENTS.md, at lines 168 and 362. The
concerns are disjoint (component lists versus plugin.json claims) but running both concurrently
against the same file invites a needless conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `grep -n "plugin.json" AGENTS.md`, when run, then no matching line instructs registering a skill, agent, or command in plugin.json.
2. Given a reader follows the AGENTS.md "Adding a New Skill" steps end to end, when they finish, then they have edited no file under .claude-plugin/.
3. Given AGENTS.md line 355, when read, then it states that components are auto-discovered from their directories and no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration.
4. Given AGENTS.md lines 529 and 537, when read, then each names the AGENTS.md component list and the README table as the registration surfaces.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- No line in AGENTS.md instructs registering a component in .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
- Line 355 describes auto-discovery and scopes plugin.json to metadata plus the hooks field.
- The "Adding a New Skill" and "Adding a New Agent" steps name the true registration surfaces.

## Note
plugin.json itself is NOT changed. The auto-discovery behavior is correct; the documentation
describing it is what is wrong.
close_reason: Fixed in 1.18.1: AGENTS.md no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration, and the Adding a New Skill/Agent steps name the real surfaces

title: Author style-testing core, reconcile style-rspec, and wire it for dispatch (Part 1)
description:
## Why (Computational)

This workbench has no framework-independent test-writing guidance. Its only test skill,
style-rspec (496 lines), is RSpec-on-Rails specific, and a grep across skills/ and hooks/ finds
zero guidance for pytest, Vitest, Jest, XCTest, Swift Testing, or Minitest. The owner works in
multiple languages and no longer uses RSpec, so the repo's richest style asset is unusable to them.

The universal core every other style skill sits on (hooks/style-core.md, 72 lines) is a
production-code core: its nine principles cover abstraction, unit size, interfaces, dependency
injection, tell-don't-ask, composition, errors, the step-down rule, and naming. None address test
structure. So the gap is not "style-rspec lacks a core" (it already points at style-core.md at
lines 27-29); it is that no testing core exists for anything to sit on.

Reaching the skill matters as much as writing it. agents/software-engineer.md:35-39 and
agents/code-reviewer.md:38-40 dispatch to style skills by file extension, and test files have no
routing entry anywhere. A skill wired only into AGENTS.md and README.md would ship unreachable,
which is exactly the state style-rspec is in today: well written, documented, never loaded.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing.md

## Estimated size
10 files, net about -57 LOC (+235 new core, -400 rspec trim, +108 wiring and gates). Band: Target.
design:
Mirror the established delta structure. Author skills/style-testing/SKILL.md as a genuine testing
core of 14 principles (10 transposed from style-rspec, 4 net-new: determinism, behavior-not-
implementation naming, what not to test, precise assertions), then rewrite style-rspec to carry
only RSpec deltas, opening with a pointer to style-testing the way style-python:26 points at
hooks/style-core.md.

Key decisions:

D2. The principles body names no framework; exactly one fenced appendix maps each principle to its
pytest, Vitest/Jest, XCTest/Swift Testing, and Minitest idiom. Without the appendix the skill is
platitudes; with it inside the principles it stops being a core. Enforced by a static check
script, not by author discipline.

D3. Keep style-rspec as a roughly 90-line delta rather than deleting it. Cheap, keeps
review-rails:30 resolving, and deletion is irreversible.

D4. No sibling delta skills (style-pytest, style-vitest). Wait for duplication before abstracting.

D6. The frontmatter description is a first-class deliverable with its own invocation test.
style-rspec's description ("RSpec tests in Rails apps") is scoped so narrowly it can never fire on
the owner's current work; that failure mode must not be reproduced.

D7. The cheap deterministic gates (static leak check, invocation test) ship here. The expensive
behavioral A/B eval ships in Part 2, so Part 1 can prove the skill is correct-by-construction,
wired, and reachable, but not that it is useful. That limitation is accepted and named.

Milestones: M1 author core; M2 rspec delta (own commit, pre-rewrite SHA captured first); M3 doc
rewire (review-rails:30, AGENTS.md:168 and :362, README.md:135); M3b dispatch rewire
(software-engineer.md:35-39 and :54, code-reviewer.md:38-40, python-feature-dev.md:13) adding test
file patterns; M5a static and invocation gates.

Supersedes this bead's original design, which assumed the owner still used RSpec and required
registering the skill in .claude-plugin/plugin.json. That file registers zero components; the
claim traces to a documentation defect in AGENTS.md, tracked separately in Part 2.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a reader opens skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, when they read the principles, anti-patterns, escape hatches, and checklist sections, then no rule names a construct from any specific test framework (definition; criterion 2 is its enforcement).
2. Given `python3 skills/style-testing/scripts/check_framework_leak.py`, when run, then it exits 0 and reports zero leaked framework tokens outside the appendix and the frontmatter.
3. Given a reader opens skills/style-rspec/SKILL.md, when they read its opening section, then it names style-testing as the core it extends, and the file is under 120 lines.
4. Given `grep -rn "style-testing" AGENTS.md README.md skills/review-rails/SKILL.md`, when run, then all three files match.
5. Given skills/review-rails/SKILL.md previously deferred test style to style-rspec, when the rewire lands, then it defers to style-testing first and names style-rspec only as the RSpec-conditional delta, and both skills still exist on disk.
6. Given the orphan check in /validate-plugin, whose rule is "skills not referenced by any agent or command", when run, then style-testing is referenced by at least one file in agents/ and is not flagged as an orphan.
7. Given the M5a invocation test, when run over its 8 test-writing prompts and 3 non-test controls, then at least 7 test prompts invoke style-testing and at most 1 control false-fires.
8. Given `git log --oneline -- skills/style-rspec/SKILL.md`, when inspected after M2, then the rewrite is an isolated commit revertible without touching M1 or M3.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- skills/style-testing/SKILL.md exists with 14 framework-free principles plus the fenced framework-idiom appendix.
- Its frontmatter description names the activity and the frameworks, so the skill can actually be invoked.
- style-rspec retains no guidance that would read as correct advice with the RSpec nouns stripped out, and is under 120 lines.
- style-testing is referenced by at least one file in agents/, so /validate-plugin does not flag it as an orphan.
- Test file patterns route to style-testing in software-engineer, code-reviewer, and python-feature-dev.
- check_framework_leak.py exits 0, and the invocation test clears 7 of 8.

## Scope boundary
Efficacy (does the skill measurably improve the tests a model writes) is deliberately NOT proven
here. That is Part 2. Part 1 ships a skill that is correct-by-construction, wired, and reachable.

## Progress (in_progress)
Done and verified: M1 (skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, 269 lines, 14 principles + fenced appendix),
M2 (style-rspec 496 -> 119 lines; baseline SHA f82c91e29a2fd395de2c77f4ab4ad5d2d4729bae; isolated
commit), M3 (AGENTS.md, README.md, review-rails), M3b (software-engineer, code-reviewer,
python-feature-dev), M5a static half (check_framework_leak.py, verified against a planted-leak
control).

Passing: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8.

## BLOCKED: AC7 needs a fresh session
The invocation battery cannot run in the session that created the skill. Claude Code loads its
skill registry at session start, so style-testing is absent from every subagent's available-skills
list until a restart. A probe subagent confirmed it: style_testing_present = false.

Running the battery now would score 0/8 for a reason unrelated to description quality, which is
what AC7 is meant to measure. Run it first thing in a new session, before any other work.
close_reason: Part 1 complete: all 8 acceptance criteria pass, including AC7 at 8/8 positive and 0/3 control
